brief.title: The three-hour window
brief.audience: Small-group travellers booking a coastal walking week
brief.objective: Book the September departure and understand why the tide, not the itinerary, sets the day
brief.visualDirection: Authored for this deck; see creativeDirection.

narrative: By the end a traveller should book September, because the causeway is only open three hours a day and September is when that window falls in daylight.

creativeDirection.name: Tide window
creativeDirection.concept: The light is the reason to go and the tide is the reason for the schedule; the deck lets the first carry the page and pins the second to the foot
creativeDirection.rationale: People book coastal walks for the atmosphere and cancel them over logistics, so both have to be on the same slide without one drowning the other
creativeDirection.geometryLanguage: Full-bleed plates and one horizontal band. No frames, no rounded corners, no floating captions
creativeDirection.spatialRhythm: Loud, quiet, loud: an atmospheric plate never follows another
creativeDirection.materialLanguage: Wet light and haze; type sits on a solid band rather than on the image itself

window.description: A horizontal bar with a lit segment
window.usage: Once, on the tide slide; never repeated as decoration

hard: Type never sits directly on an image without a solid band behind it
Every time given is a predicted time and says so
soft: Let one plate per slide be the only picture

title: The three-hour window
designIntent: Show the place first. The title sits in a solid band at the foot so it is legible without dimming the plate.
composition: Edge-to-edge plate; a single dark band across the bottom fifth carrying the title and one line.

alt: A pale estuary horizon with the water darkening toward the foreground

provenance.source: Abstract estuary horizon generated for this showcase; not a photograph of a real place

text: A five-day coastal walk timed to the tide, not to the timetable.

notes: Say nothing for the first few seconds.

title: When the sea lets you across
designIntent: One bar, one lit segment. The constraint is a shape before it is a number.
composition: A wide horizontal bar across the middle; hours labelled beneath; nothing above it but the title.

text: When the sea lets you across
The causeway is safe for about three hours either side of low water. Everything else in the week is arranged around that.
Times are predictions. The harbour office posts the day's window each morning and it is the one that counts.
Admiralty tide tables 2026, station 0412; safe-crossing margins as published by the harbour office.

notes: If one thing survives the meeting, it should be this shape.

title: Five days, sixty-one kilometres
designIntent: The itinerary without a table. Five thin rows, each with its distance set right so the eye can total them.
composition: Five full-width rows down the page; distances aligned at the right edge.

notes: Wednesday is short on purpose — it is the only day the window is late.

title: September, and only September
designIntent: The emotional argument, but load-bearing: the plate is on the left and the reason is on the right, at reading size.
composition: A plate filling the left half; type in a column on the right, with a band behind nothing.

alt: A warm low sun over a harbour, the light falling from the upper right

provenance.source: Abstract harbour light field generated for this showcase; not a photograph of a real place

text: In September the low-water window falls in daylight on all five days. In June it falls before dawn twice; in November the crossing is dark on the way back. The walk exists in other months. The light does not.
Derived from the 2026 tide tables and civil twilight for 54.1°N.

notes: This is the slide that sells the week. Do not rush it.

title: What people actually ask
designIntent: Quiet and useful. The plate is absent on purpose — this slide is for the questions that stop a booking.
composition: A table filling the upper two-thirds under a short title; a single caution beneath it.

rows: Yes. The window closes about three hours after low water.
Wait for the next window; there is a tea room and it is six hours.
Firm sand and shingle; two short scrambles on Thursday.
Thursday's circuit can be shortened to 8 km.
What if the ferry is cancelled?
It happens roughly one Friday in six.
A road transfer is included in the price, not extra.
Carry a day pack with water and a shell.

text: Nothing on this slide is a guarantee about the sea. Every crossing is decided on the morning, by the harbour office, not by the itinerary.

notes: Read the caution aloud. It is the sentence that keeps everyone safe and it is also why people trust the rest.

title: 12 September
designIntent: One date, at display size, low on an empty page. The risk is named beside it rather than buried.
composition: A single line at the lower left; the honest caveat set small at the right.

text: Eight places. Five walking days. One tide table.
The honest risk: one Friday in six the ferry does not run, and roughly one crossing a season is called off entirely. Both are covered by the road transfer, and neither is refunded as a lost day.

notes: End on the risk, not the price. It is what makes the date credible.
